cases.title: Pagination returns the second page for page 1

input.task: paginate() gives me the wrong page. page 1 comes back as what should be page 2. not sure what happens with page 0 either

reference.root_cause: paginate() computes the slice start as page * per_page, which treats pages as 0-indexed, so page 1 returns the second page; it also never rejects page < 1.
reference.fix_summary: Compute start as (page - 1) * per_page and raise ValueError when page < 1.
reference.reference_diff:
diff --git a/pagination.py b/pagination.py
--- a/pagination.py
+++ b/pagination.py
@@ -1,4 +1,6 @@
 def paginate(items, page, per_page):
     """Return the items on the given 1-indexed page."""
-    start = page * per_page
+    if page < 1:
+        raise ValueError("page must be >= 1")
+    start = (page - 1) * per_page
     return items[start:start + per_page]

cases.title: Invoice totals off by a cent, negative totals

input.task: finance keeps flagging invoices that are a cent off and one customer got a negative total after using a coupon. can someone look at invoice.py

reference.root_cause: invoice_total() does money maths in binary floats and subtracts the coupon after tax, so cents drift, a coupon is taxed incorrectly and can push the total below zero.
reference.fix_summary: Use Decimal, subtract the coupon from the subtotal first, clamp at zero, apply tax, quantize to cents with ROUND_HALF_UP.
reference.reference_diff:
diff --git a/invoice.py b/invoice.py
--- a/invoice.py
+++ b/invoice.py
@@ -1,5 +1,9 @@
+from decimal import Decimal, ROUND_HALF_UP
+
+
 def invoice_total(lines, coupon="0", tax_rate="0"):
     """Total for (unit_price, qty) lines after a money coupon and a tax rate."""
-    subtotal = sum(float(price) * qty for price, qty in lines)
-    total = subtotal * (1 + float(tax_rate)) - float(coupon)
-    return round(total, 2)
+    subtotal = sum((Decimal(price) * qty for price, qty in lines), Decimal("0"))
+    discounted = max(subtotal - Decimal(coupon), Decimal("0"))
+    total = discounted * (1 + Decimal(tax_rate))
+    return total.quantize(Decimal("0.01"), rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)

cases.title: Release list in a weird order

input.task: releases page order is wrong. 1.10 shows up before 1.9 and the rc builds are listed after the final release. keep the tags as written please

reference.root_cause: sort_versions() sorts the raw strings lexicographically, so 1.10 sorts before 1.9, release candidates sort after the final release and a leading 'v' changes the order.
reference.fix_summary: Sort with a key that strips a leading v, compares numeric components, ignores trailing zeros and puts pre-releases before the release; keep the original strings.

diff --git a/versions.py b/versions.py
--- a/versions.py
+++ b/versions.py
@@ -1,3 +1,10 @@
 def sort_versions(versions):
     """Return the version strings sorted from oldest to newest."""
-    return sorted(versions)
+    def key(v):
+        text = v[1:] if v[:1] in ("v", "V") else v
+        core, _, pre = text.partition("-")
+        nums = [int(p) for p in core.split(".")]
+        while nums and nums[-1] == 0:
+            nums.pop()
+        return (nums, 0 if pre else 1, pre)
+    return sorted(versions, key=key)

cases.title: Cache evicts hot entries

input.task: cache is dropping things we literally just read, and a worker with cache size 0 crashes on its first write.

reference.root_cause: LRUCache never tracks recency: get() does not refresh the entry, put() of an existing key evicts another entry when full, and capacity 0 crashes on the first write.
reference.fix_summary: Use an OrderedDict, move keys to the end on get and update, evict only for new keys, and ignore writes when capacity <= 0.
reference.reference_diff:
diff --git a/lru.py b/lru.py
--- a/lru.py
+++ b/lru.py
@@ -1,17 +1,26 @@
+from collections import OrderedDict
+
+
 class LRUCache:
     """Least-recently-used cache with a fixed capacity."""
 
     def __init__(self, capacity):
         self.capacity = capacity
-        self.data = {}
+        self.data = OrderedDict()
 
     def get(self, key, default=None):
-        return self.data.get(key, default)
+        if key not in self.data:
+            return default
+        self.data.move_to_end(key)
+        return self.data[key]
 
     def put(self, key, value):
-        if len(self.data) >= self.capacity:
-            oldest = next(iter(self.data))
-            del self.data[oldest]
+        if self.capacity <= 0:
+            return
+        if key in self.data:
+            self.data.move_to_end(key)
+        elif len(self.data) >= self.capacity:
+            self.data.popitem(last=False)
         self.data[key] = value
 
     def __len__(self):
key_facts: updating an existing key never evicts another entry
capacity 0 stores nothing and does not crash

cases.title: Back-to-back bookings rejected

input.task: can't book 10-11 right after a 9-10 meeting, it says conflict

reference.root_cause: overlaps() uses <= comparisons although bookings are half-open [start, end) intervals, so back-to-back bookings are reported as conflicts.
reference.fix_summary: Use strict < comparisons in overlaps() so touching intervals do not overlap.
reference.reference_diff:
diff --git a/booking/intervals.py b/booking/intervals.py
--- a/booking/intervals.py
+++ b/booking/intervals.py
@@ -3,4 +3,4 @@
 
 def overlaps(a_start, a_end, b_start, b_end):
     """True when the two half-open intervals share any time. Back-to-back intervals do not overlap."""
-    return a_start <= b_end and b_start <= a_end
+    return a_start < b_end and b_start < a_end

--- a/wordstats/tokenizer.py
+++ b/wordstats/tokenizer.py
@@ -4,4 +4,4 @@
 
 def tokenize(text):
     """Lower-case words; an apostrophe inside a word (don't) stays part of the word."""
-    return re.findall(r"[A-Za-z]+", text)
+    return re.findall(r"[a-z]+(?:'[a-z]+)?", text.lower())
